capture.final_message:
Write a distinguished triangle as
\[
X \xrightarrow f Y \xrightarrow g Z \xrightarrow h X[1].
\]
Use the exact sequence obtained by applying each representable functor \(\operatorname{Hom}(W,-)\), together with rotation of the triangle.

This single mechanism gives all four universal assertions:

- If \(h=0\), exactness at \(\operatorname{Hom}(W,X)\) makes postcomposition with \(f\) injective for every \(W\); hence \(f\) is mono.
- If \(g\) is an isomorphism, the triangle identities give \(f=h=0\). Exactness then forces every \(\operatorname{Hom}(W,X)\) to vanish, so \(X\) is zero by Yoneda.
- More generally, \(X\) is zero exactly when \(f=0\) and \(h=0\): one direction is immediate, while the other is the same exactness-and-Yoneda argument.
- If \(X\) and \(Z\) are zero, exactness of
  \[
  \operatorname{Hom}(W,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,Z)
  \]
  forces \(\operatorname{Hom}(W,Y)=0\) for every \(W\), hence \(Y\) is zero.

Thus prove these standard triangle lemmas once—preferably using Mathlib’s existing exactness results for distinguished triangles and their rotations—and assemble the two `Iff`s from the corresponding universally valid statements. The essential assumption is pretriangulated exactness; the zero object and Yoneda convert vanishing representable Hom groups into `IsZero`.
